title: Automated Personalized Feedback Improves Learning Gains in an Intelligent Tutoring System
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether automatically generated, data-driven personalized feedback can improve student learning in an intelligent tutoring system (ITS). The authors focus on the challenge of producing useful hints and explanations at scale without relying on hand-authored rules or expert intervention, and they evaluate whether different feedback-generation strategies lead to better learning outcomes.

The intervention is implemented in Korbit, a large-scale dialogue-based ITS that combines machine learning, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. The system generates multiple forms of feedback, including personalized hints and explanations, Wikipedia-based explanations, and mathematical hints. The study compares baseline, shallow personalization, and deep personalization models for selecting feedback, and also reports analyses of Wikipedia-based explanations and mathematical hints.

The empirical evaluation used 796 annotated student-system interactions from 183 students enrolled in a free machine learning course on the Korbit platform between January and February 2020. The paper reports that deep personalization produced the highest learning gains, with a statistically significant advantage over the baseline in some comparisons, and that students generally rated the generated explanations as helpful. The authors conclude that automated personalized feedback can substantially improve learning gains and appears promising for scalable ITS support.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed empirical system study with annotated interaction data and a comparison between feedback conditions, but it is not a randomized controlled trial and relies on historical/observational interaction data with limited methodological detail. The reported significance test and confidence intervals strengthen credibility, but causal inference remains moderate.
impact_tier_rationale: The intervention shows modest-to-strong positive learning gains in a large-scale tutoring platform, with gains of roughly 9-23 percentage points depending on comparison and timing. However, the evidence is from a single platform and domain, and the strongest reported outcome is a process measure rather than a standardized achievement test.

interventions.use_case: large-scale dialogue-based intelligent tutoring system with automated personalized hints, explanations, Wikipedia-based explanations, and mathematical hints for students solving machine learning/data science exercises
machine-learned personalized feedback selection and generation for incorrect student solutions, including hints and explanations tailored to the student's recent interaction history

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports improved student learning gains after receiving automated personalized feedback in Korbit. Across 796 annotated student-system interactions from 183 students, deep personalization achieved 48.53% learning gain for all attempts versus 39.47% for the baseline, and 60.47% versus 37.93% before the second attempt; the latter difference was statistically significant (z-test p=0.03005).
finding.measure: Proportion of instances where a student provided a correct solution after receiving a personalized hint or explanation
finding.confidence_interval: [44.41%, 75.02%] for deep personalization before second attempt; baseline [20.69%, 57.74%]

finding.finding_summary: The paper also found that automatically generated Wikipedia-based explanations produced learning gains comparable to the other feedback conditions. Students rated either or both types of explanations as helpful 83.33% of the time, suggesting the explanations were perceived as useful and supportive of learning.
finding.measure: Learning gain following Wikipedia-based explanations; subjective helpfulness ratings

finding.finding_summary: The feedback intervention appears to support problem-solving and response revision during tutoring, which is a durable-skill-adjacent process, though this was not directly isolated as a separate construct. The paper does not report a dedicated standardized measure of metacognition or critical thinking; evidence is indirect from improved post-feedback correctness rates.
